text: Q1 — When a type has a registered view, how does the promoted structure relate to the rendered markdown body?
answer: View is primary, source behind a toggle
options: View is primary, source behind a toggle
Structured lead, full document always below
raw:
### Q1 — When a type has a registered view, how does the promoted structure relate to the rendered markdown body?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| View is primary, source behind a toggle | The per-type view IS the page; full rendered markdown reachable via an explicit "Document source" toggle. Avoids double-rendering. Costs: the view must not silently drop unpromoted content. | ✓ |
| Structured lead, full document always below | Keeps Phase 2's D-09 shape exactly. Nothing can be lost; a thin manifest degrades gracefully. Costs: duplication on all 12 section-projection types. | |
| Per-type manifest decides | Manifest declares its own mode — lead-then-body for frontmatter types, replace-with-toggle for section types. More faithful, one more axis per manifest. | |
**User's choice:** View is primary, source behind a toggle

text: Q2 — A manifest promotes some sections/fields. What happens to everything it doesn't promote?
options: Renders after, in document order, inside the view
raw:
### Q2 — A manifest promotes some sections/fields. What happens to everything it doesn't promote?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Renders after, in document order, inside the view | Promoted structure first, then remaining content in original order. Nothing lost even with a thin manifest. | |
| Only in the source toggle | View shows exactly what the manifest promotes. Sharpest views, but a stale manifest silently hides content as GSD evolves. | |
| Renders after, collapsed by default | Unpromoted content present but folded behind a disclosure. Keeps the view tight while guaranteeing nothing is unreachable. Costs an extra click. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Renders after, collapsed by default

text: Q3 — What does the "Document source" escape hatch actually show?
options: Literal raw markdown in a code block
raw:
### Q3 — What does the "Document source" escape hatch actually show?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| The v1.0 generic rendered document | Full document through the existing sanitized markdown pipeline — tables, code, Mermaid, anchors, linkified mentions intact. | ✓ |
| Literal raw markdown in a code block | Verbatim file text, no rendering. Zero interpretation; loses tables/diagrams/links. | |
| Both, as two toggle states | Most complete, but three states on every document page for a single-user tool. | |
**User's choice:** The v1.0 generic rendered document

text: Q1 — Within the promoted region, may a manifest order things differently from the file?
options: No — promoted items keep file order
Yes, and views may also re-rank by status
raw:
### Q1 — Within the promoted region, may a manifest order things differently from the file?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Yes — manifest declares promotion order | The promotion list IS the order. VIEW-03's "leads with what needs a human" becomes a one-line manifest fact rather than special-case code. | ✓ |
| No — promoted items keep file order | Simplest to reason about, hardest to misrepresent a document — but VIEW-03 would need the source file to already lead with human checks, which it doesn't. | |
| Yes, and views may also re-rank by status | Failing checks above passing, unselected options below the chosen one. Most useful at a glance, most interpretation layered over the file. | |
**User's choice:** Yes — manifest declares promotion order

text: Q2 — The view now departs from file order. How does the page stay honest about that?
answer: Source toggle is the only signal
options: Each promoted block links to its source position
Source toggle is the only signal
raw:
### Q2 — The view now departs from file order. How does the page stay honest about that?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Each promoted block links to its source position | A quiet "in document" affordance resolving to the heading anchor; reuses rehype-slug anchors and the D-16 copy-link pattern. Auditable per item. | |
| Source toggle is the only signal | No per-block provenance; flip to Document source for the file's own order. Cleanest surface, uncluttered by meta-affordances. | ✓ |
| One provenance note per page | A single `source-note`-style line stating what was promoted and that the remainder follows. | |
**User's choice:** Source toggle is the only signal

text: Q3 — A manifest promotes a section or field that this particular file doesn't have. What does the view do?
options: Show the slot with an empty state
Omit, but mark the document as partially matched
raw:
### Q3 — A manifest promotes a section or field that this particular file doesn't have. What does the view do?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Silently omit it | Absence is normal — GSD templates carry optional sections and the corpus is full of legitimately partial artifacts. Matches the v1.0 rule that dangling references are data, not warnings. | ✓ |
| Show the slot with an empty state | Distinguishes "no human checks" from "the view didn't look". Costs empty scaffolding on every partial document. | |
| Omit, but mark the document as partially matched | A quiet "matched N of M" chip signalling manifest drift without cluttering the body. | |
**User's choice:** Silently omit it

text: Q1 — Where does the written design language live?
raw:
### Q1 — Where does the written design language live?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Repo doc + CLAUDE.md pointer | A real document owns the vocabulary; § Conventions in CLAUDE.md shrinks to a one-line pointer that survives regeneration. | ✓ |
| Inside `.claude/CLAUDE.md` § Conventions | Unavoidably in context when writing a new view. Risk: GSD-managed section, may be clobbered, bloats every prompt. | |
| Co-located with the CSS | Closest to the selectors it describes, least likely to drift — furthest from where a planning agent looks. | |
**User's choice:** Repo doc + CLAUDE.md pointer

text: Q2 — UI-05 says a test must stop a new view from silently drifting. What does that test actually block?
raw:
### Q2 — UI-05 says a test must stop a new view from silently drifting. What does that test actually block?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Class vocabulary allowlist | Derives sanctioned names from the doc, scans `className` literals, fails on anything outside the vocabulary. Forces reuse or an explicit doc amendment. | ✓ |
| Token/primitive lint only | Fails on raw hex/rgb, hardcoded px, non-token spacing. Cheap and zero false positives, but doesn't stop a view inventing its own heading or chip pattern. | |
| Structural conformance per registered view | Every registry entry must render the shared page skeleton. Tests shape rather than strings; weaker against bespoke chrome added on top. | |
**User's choice:** Class vocabulary allowlist

text: Q3 — How does a view legitimately introduce a class name the vocabulary doesn't have?
options: Doc amendment is the only route
raw:
### Q3 — How does a view legitimately introduce a class name the vocabulary doesn't have?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Reserved view-local namespace | Names under a declared per-view prefix are auto-allowed as view-private; anything else needs a doc amendment. Every shared name stays a deliberate act. | ✓ |
| Doc amendment is the only route | Maximum pressure toward reuse and a genuinely complete vocabulary. Costs friction on every internal element, 16 views over. | |
| Exception list in the test | Visible and greppable in one place — but a second vocabulary that drifts from the doc. | |
**User's choice:** Reserved view-local namespace

text: Q4 — Does the vocabulary test also run over the existing dashboard, roadmap, traceability and search pages?
answer: Yes — they're the reference, so they must pass
options: Yes — they're the reference, so they must pass
Yes, but reference-page failures are warnings
raw:
### Q4 — Does the vocabulary test also run over the existing dashboard, roadmap, traceability and search pages?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Yes — they're the reference, so they must pass | The doc is derived from them, so they pass by construction; a failure means the vocabulary was written incompletely. Also stops the reference itself drifting. | ✓ |
| Document views only | Smallest blast radius; no risk of the phase turning into cleanup of out-of-scope pages. | |
| Yes, but reference-page failures are warnings | Two severities in one test — surfaces reference drift without blocking on pre-existing conditions. | |
**User's choice:** Yes — they're the reference, so they must pass

text: Q1 — What does the outline list now that the page is a view rather than a plain document?
options: View sections, plus document headings nested under them
raw:
### Q1 — What does the outline list now that the page is a view rather than a plain document?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| The view's own sections | Mirrors what's on screen — promoted sections in promotion order, then the collapsed remainder as one entry. Stays truthful under reordering; the registry already knows the section list. | ✓ |
| Document headings, as today | Zero change to the data source and matches the Document-source view exactly — but would list headings the view has reordered or folded away. | |
| View sections, plus document headings nested under them | Richest navigation on long artifacts. More machinery, and the 18-entry cap gets tight fast. | |
**User's choice:** The view's own sections

text: Q2 — READ-07 says the outline stays legible at every viewport width. What happens when the sticky left column doesn't fit?
answer: Collapses to a sticky disclosure above the document
options: Collapses to a sticky disclosure above the document
Moves into normal flow above the document
Folds into the existing sidebar drawer
raw:
### Q2 — READ-07 says the outline stays legible at every viewport width. What happens when the sticky left column doesn't fit?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Collapses to a sticky disclosure above the document | Pinned under the page chrome; opening overlays the section list. Reachable at any scroll depth without eating width; reuses the existing disclosure pattern. | ✓ |
| Moves into normal flow above the document | Simplest possible behaviour — but on a long artifact only reachable by scrolling back to the top, which is most of what READ-07 is complaining about. | |
| Folds into the existing sidebar drawer | One narrow-width navigation surface instead of two; mixes cross-document with in-document navigation. | |
**User's choice:** Collapses to a sticky disclosure above the document

text: Q3 — How does the outline show reading position?
answer: Active highlight, and the collapsed label names it
options: Active highlight, and the collapsed label names it
raw:
### Q3 — How does the outline show reading position?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Active highlight, and the collapsed label names it | One active entry via IntersectionObserver, and at narrow width the disclosure label reads "On this page · <current section>". Position answerable without opening anything. | ✓ |
| Active highlight only | Smallest surface, one behaviour to test. At narrow width you learn nothing until you open it. | |
| Active highlight plus passed-section treatment | Reads as progress through the document; another visual state to hold consistent across light and dark. | |
**User's choice:** Active highlight, and the collapsed label names it

text: Q4 — Given D-XX and WR-XX are phase-scoped, how does a mention resolve?
options: Resolve within the containing phase only
Phase-local, with a disambiguating preview when ambiguous
raw:
### Q4 — Given D-XX and WR-XX are phase-scoped, how does a mention resolve?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Resolve within the containing phase only | Matches how the IDs are authored, so it's right by default and never links to the wrong phase's decision. A mention outside any phase directory stays plain text per D-17. | |
| Phase-local first, then whole corpus | Try the containing phase; fall back to a corpus-wide search and link if exactly one match exists. Catches cross-phase citations in PROJECT.md and MILESTONES.md. | ✓ |
| Phase-local, with a disambiguating preview when ambiguous | Never guesses wrong, but builds a second preview shape just for the ambiguous case. | |
**User's choice:** Phase-local first, then whole corpus

text: Q5 — D-14 locked preview-first for requirement, phase and plan IDs. Do D-XX and WR-XX follow that pattern?
options: Yes for decisions, direct navigation for warnings
raw:
### Q5 — D-14 locked preview-first for requirement, phase and plan IDs. Do D-XX and WR-XX follow that pattern?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Yes — same preview, decision/warning-shaped detail | Reuses `reference-preview.tsx`; the type-specific detail is the decision statement or finding title plus the defining phase — exactly the disambiguation the global fallback needs. | ✓ |
| Yes for decisions, direct navigation for warnings | Fits how the two are used, at the cost of two behaviours for visually identical tokens. | |
| Direct navigation for both | Fewer steps when you know you want the source; departs from D-14, so the document surface would behave differently from the rest of the app. | |
**User's choice:** Yes — same preview, decision/warning-shaped detail

text: Q1 — How should the dense fixture be constructed?
raw:
### Q1 — How should the dense fixture be constructed?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Hand-authored synthetic | Shape derived from `~/.claude/gsd-core/templates/`, not studio-portal. Full control; can include `AI-SPEC.md`/`SPEC.md`, a third milestone, an invented future type. Costs authoring time; files are stubby rather than realistic in length. | ✓ |
| Redacted studio-portal copy | Real structure with placeholder bodies. Realistic scale and naming edge cases for free, but inherits studio-portal's exact artifact set — the shape research warns against overfitting to. | |
| Generated by running gsd-core | Real gsd-core 1.11.0 output; truest fidelity, sparse fixture nearly free. But driving it to genuinely dense means running a lot of workflow, and it cannot produce types GSD doesn't ship yet. | |
| Hand-authored, seeded from templates | Mechanically copy every template file as a skeleton, then hand-edit. Traceability to template lines by construction. | |
**User's choice:** Hand-authored synthetic

text: Q2 — Where does the deliberately corrupted content live?
options: Both — seeded dense plus a broken one
raw:
### Q2 — Where does the deliberately corrupted content live?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Inside the dense fixture | Broken files among healthy ones. Truest to Criterion 3's "while every other file parses cleanly". Cost: dense golden permanently contains warnings. | ✓ |
| A third, purely-broken fixture | Keeps both goldens pristine and assertable at zero warnings; gives Phase 4 an obvious target. Cost: exceeds DATA-06's "two fixtures"; isolation-among-healthy-files not directly proven. | |
| Both — seeded dense plus a broken one | Most thorough; cleanly splits degradation from refusal. Cost: three fixtures to author and maintain. | |

text: Q3 — How do we resolve the sparse-fixture contradiction between Phase 1 SC2 and Phase 4 SC1?
raw:
### Q3 — How do we resolve the sparse-fixture contradiction between Phase 1 SC2 and Phase 4 SC1?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Two sparse variants | Empty-floor tree plus barely-started tree. Different code paths; each roadmap criterion gets the fixture it names. Cost: three trees total, extending DATA-06's "two". | ✓ |
| Empty floor only | Honors Phase 1's wording; harshest input, exercises every null-check. Cost: the "structure but no history" path — the common early-project case — goes untested. | |
| One phase, no milestones only | Honors Phase 4's wording; more representative of daily use. Cost: the true empty-project path goes untested, which PITFALLS #1 calls out by name. | |

text: Q4 — What role does `~/studio-portal` play in Phase 1's verification?
raw:
### Q4 — What role does `~/studio-portal` play in Phase 1's verification?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Manual smoke target only | Fixtures are the committed asserted suite; studio-portal is eyeballed by hand with no committed assertions. Keeps the machine-checked contract fixture-derived. Cost: real-world-only regressions aren't caught automatically. | ✓ |
| Committed golden snapshot too | Catches real-corpus regressions automatically. Cost: enormous golden, constant churn (studio-portal is actively worked), non-portable test suite. | |
| Smoke target with invariant-only assertions | Asserts only churn-proof shape invariants; skips cleanly when the directory is absent. Cost: one more harness mode to build and keep honest. | |
**User's choice:** Manual smoke target only

text: Q1 — What is the harness, concretely?
options: CLI, goldens, and a summary mode
raw:
### Q1 — What is the harness, concretely?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| CLI plus golden tests | `npm run snapshot -- <path>` prints JSON; Vitest suite invokes the same entry point against fixtures and diffs a committed golden. Shared entry point prevents the tested path diverging from the runnable one. | ✓ |
| CLI only | Simplest thing satisfying DATA-05's literal wording; no goldens to churn. Cost: no automatic regression catching — verification becomes a human reading a large JSON blob. | |
| Golden tests only | Least code; `vitest -u` regenerates on intentional change. Cost: no ergonomic way to target an arbitrary path, making TGT-01/TGT-02's path-form proof awkward. | |
| CLI, goldens, and a summary mode | Adds a compact human digest — counts by kind, tree outline, warnings, unresolved refs. Cost: a second output format to keep in sync. | |
**User's choice:** CLI plus golden tests

text: Q2 — Does the dumped JSON include every artifact's full markdown body?
answer: Omit bodies by default, flag to include
options: Omit bodies by default, flag to include
raw:
### Q2 — Does the dumped JSON include every artifact's full markdown body?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Omit bodies by default, flag to include | Structure, frontmatter, cross-refs, warnings, plus body length and hash. Readable diffs; hash catches truncation. Cost: length-preserving body mangling invisible without the flag. | ✓ |
| Always include full bodies | Most literal reading of DATA-05; golden genuinely proves nothing is lost. Cost: large goldens, unreadable diffs, one-character prose edits rewriting the file. | |
| Never include bodies | Smallest cleanest goldens. Cost: Criterion 3's "degrades to its raw body" becomes uncheckable through the harness. | |
**User's choice:** Omit bodies by default, flag to include

text: Q3 — How does the harness handle machine-varying values in golden output?
options: Keep paths relative in the model itself
raw:
### Q3 — How does the harness handle machine-varying values in golden output?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Normalize in a serializer | One step replaces absolute paths with root-relative and mtimes with a placeholder under `--stable`; raw CLI dump keeps real values. All machine-variance owned in one function. | ✓ |
| Keep paths relative in the model itself | Path variance disappears at the source; makes containment checks natural. Mtimes still need handling. Cost: re-joining to root wherever a real path is needed. | |
| Both | Model clean by construction plus serializer protection for future volatile fields. Cost: more ceremony for a currently two-field problem. | |
**User's choice:** Normalize in a serializer

### Q4 — How is Criterion 4 (swappable filesystem) proven rather than asserted?
| Option | Description | Selected |

| In-memory FS fixture implementation | A second `PlanningFilesystem` over a `path → content` map runs the same golden tests; byte-identical output proves the seam by construction. Also speeds fixture tests and enables hostile cases awkward to commit. | ✓ |

text: Q1 — Where do warnings live on the snapshot?
raw:
### Q1 — Where do warnings live on the snapshot?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Both root list and artifact | Flat `snapshot.warnings[]` plus a per-artifact reference. Same objects, two access paths. Cost: two places to keep consistent, so both must be built from one source. | ✓ |
| Root list only | One source of truth, trivially serializable. Cost: pushes the path-filter join onto every consumer. | |
| On the artifact only | Degradation sits next to the thing degraded. Cost: warnings belonging to no artifact — an unlistable directory, an unreadable file that never became an artifact — have nowhere to live. | |

### Q2 — Are unresolvable cross-references warnings?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Separate — not warnings | `{ raw, resolved: null }` on the graph, out of the warning channel. Dangling refs are expected, not exceptional. Cost: a typo'd ID looks identical to a deliberately-unlinked mention. | ✓ |
| Warnings at an info severity | One channel with a severity field; ready-made health feed. Cost: info tier dominates by an order of magnitude, making warning counts meaningless without filtering. | |
| Separate, plus a rollup count | Keeps the channel meaningful while surfacing "47 dangling IDs" at a glance. Cost: one more derived field to keep accurate. | |

text: Q4 — What does the read layer return when the target isn't a GSD project?
raw:
### Q4 — What does the read layer return when the target isn't a GSD project?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| A snapshot with a `loadStatus` field | `load()` always resolves; status is `ok`/`not-a-gsd-project`/`path-not-found`/`permission-denied` plus the exact path checked. One shape for every consumer; Phase 4's error screens are just another render. Cost: consumers must check rather than being forced by an exception. | ✓ |

raw:
### Q1: Day-one cp method
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Plain cp from sibling path | `cp ../michelle_ngo_four/src/lib/data/videos.json src/lib/data/videos.json` once in the plan task. Simple, transparent, leaves a real commit. Aligns with how `_four`'s files were mirrored in Phase 1. | ✓ |
| Wrap in pnpm sync:videos script | Add a `pnpm sync:videos` script that copies from a hardcoded sibling path. Same effect as cp but documented and re-runnable. Slight risk of treating the script as "the sync" instead of human review. | |
| Git subtree from _four | Use `git subtree add` to track `_four/src/lib/data/`. Preserves provenance via git history. Heavy machinery for one file; subtrees are notoriously easy to misuse. | |
| Fetch by raw GitHub URL at build | Skip checking videos.json into `_three`'s repo; fetch from `_four`'s main raw URL at build start. Maximal freshness, but breaks "static repo" posture and adds a build-time network dep. | |
**User's choice:** Plain cp (Recommended)

raw:
### Q2: Ongoing sync mechanism
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Manual cp + PR per change | Human runs the cp, opens a PR titled "sync: pull _four videos.json @ <SHA>". Cross-repo drift CI catches drift if forgotten. | ✓ |
| pnpm sync:videos script + manual PR | Same as above but run a documented script instead of raw cp. Script logs the source path + `_four` commit SHA into the PR body for traceability. | |
| GitHub Action that auto-PRs on _four push | On every push to `_four`'s main, an Action opens a PR in `_three` with the updated videos.json. Automates the catch but adds cross-repo permissions/maintenance. | |
| Cron / scheduled sync check | Nightly Action checks for drift and opens a PR if found. Latency-tolerant but adds a scheduled job to maintain. | |
**User's choice:** Manual cp + PR per change (Recommended)

### Q3: Canonical source-of-truth direction
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| _four is always canonical | PROJECT.md L110 + DATA-01 already say so. `_three` only ever pulls. After cutover, the losing repo is abandoned, so direction stops mattering. | ✓ |
| Either can be canonical with marker | Add an `// canonical: _four` comment in both repos' videos.json. If a future content edit happens in `_three` first by accident, the marker makes the inversion explicit. | |
| Shared schema repo (new package) | Extract videos.json + schema into a separate small repo, both siblings depend on it. Cleanest but heavy infra. | |

### Q4: SHA pinning storage location
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Sidecar file (`.videos-source-sha`) | Header comment in videos.json impossible (DATA-01 byte-identity). Sidecar with SHA + sync date next to videos.json. | ✓ |

### Q14: Failure classification strategy
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Retry 3× with backoff, then classify by final response | 401/403 = disabled (fail); 404 = removed (fail); 5xx/network = transient (warn, don't fail). | ✓ |
| Single attempt, any non-2xx is hard fail | Simplest. Brittle to transient hiccups. May produce flaky builds. | |
| Two passes — fast first, deep second | HEAD then full GET on failures. Reduces bandwidth but adds complexity. | |
| Treat all failures as warnings | Never fail the build. Defeats the goal. | |

| Option | Description | Selected |

| Sequential (1 at a time) | Safest for rate limits. ~17s of network. | |
| Unbounded Promise.all | Fastest (~1s). Likely trips Vimeo's per-IP throttle. | |
**User's choice:** Concurrency limit 6, per-host (Recommended)

### Q1: What file extensions should the glob accept for thumbnails?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| PNG only (`./work/*.png`) | Locks the format contract for v1.1. Trivial slug-extraction regex. | ✓ |
| Permissive (`./work/*.{jpg,jpeg,png,webp,avif}`) | Future-proof for real JPG photos. Risk of silent collision if two files share a slug. | |
| Any (`./work/*`) | Maximally permissive (matches IMG-03 literal wording). Risk of stray `.DS_Store` breaking the map. | |
**User's choice:** PNG only (`./work/*.png`)

text: Q2: How strict should the slug ↔ filename binding be?
answer: Exact: filename basename must equal slug
options: Exact: filename basename must equal slug
raw:
### Q2: How strict should the slug ↔ filename binding be?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Exact: filename basename must equal slug | `src/lib/images/work/{slug}.png` required. Build invariant compares glob keys vs `projects[].slug` — mismatch fails. | ✓ |
| Loose: filename prefix matches slug | Flexible but ambiguous — first match wins; hidden ordering dependency. | |
| Manifest-driven: explicit slug → filename mapping | Decouples slug from filename. Cost: another swap-time edit (DISC-04 anti-pattern). | |
**User's choice:** Exact: filename basename must equal slug

text: Q3: What `import.meta.glob` options should the loader use?
options: Forced srcset widths/formats via inline query params
raw:
### Q3: What `import.meta.glob` options should the loader use?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `{ query: '?enhanced', eager: true, import: 'default' }` | Matches IMG-03; `eager: true` mandatory for static prerender; `import: 'default'` for clean consumer ergonomics. | ✓ |
| `{ query: '?enhanced', eager: true }` (no `import` key) | Map values are `{ default: Picture }` modules; consumers write `.default` everywhere. | |
| Forced srcset widths/formats via inline query params | Overrides enhanced-img's auto responsive sizing; generally unnecessary. | |
**User's choice:** `{ query: '?enhanced', eager: true, import: 'default' }`

text: Q4: How should `thumbnails.ts` derive the slug key from each glob entry's path?
raw:
### Q4: How should `thumbnails.ts` derive the slug key from each glob entry's path?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Regex on the path: `/([^/]+)\.png$/` | Explicit, locally readable, one regex per format. | ✓ |
| `path.basename` + `path.extname` (Node `path` module) | More portable; pulls in `node:path` SSR-only-ish dep. | |
| Iterate + split on `/` and `.` | Hand-rolled string manipulation; same outcome with more code. | |
**User's choice:** Regex on the path: `/([^/]+)\.png$/`

text: Q1 — What does a v1 forge roll cost?
raw:
### Q1 — What does a v1 forge roll cost?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Token-only | 1 Module Token per roll. Matches MOD-03 literally; tokens stay the scarce milestone reward. Simplest. Energy's only v1 sink remains the Phase 4 Activation boost. | |
| Token + Energy | Token gates the roll AND Energy is also consumed. Adds a second Energy sink but complicates command + history (two payment fields). | |
| Both paths (Token OR Energy) | Two separate forge paths: a Token roll (free choose-one-of-three) and an Energy roll (escalating cost, scalable). Most flexible but doubles command surface. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Both paths (Token OR Energy)

text: Q2 — How do the Token and Energy paths differ in v1?
raw:
### Q2 — How do the Token and Energy paths differ in v1?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Same pool, diff cost | Same 3-choice curated pool. Token = fixed 1-token cost; Energy = escalating cost per forge. One reward pool, two cost models — unified content + history. | ✓ |
| Diff pools (Token=better) | Token rolls draw from a better/curated pool; Energy from baseline. Tokens buy rarity/quality. Needs two pool definitions. | |
| Energy roll + Token as modifier | Energy is the default path; Token is a reroll/boost currency, not a separate roll. Fewer code paths but differs from MOD-03's "spend a token on a forge roll". | |
**User's choice:** Same pool, diff cost

text: Q3 — What drives the escalating Energy cost?
raw:
### Q3 — What drives the escalating Energy cost?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Lifetime forgeCount curve | `base + forgeCount × step` (e.g. 50 + forgeCount×25). Permanently escalates with the never-resetting forgeCount. Tokens stay relevant forever. No new counter. | ✓ |
| Per-day resetting curve | Escalates within a session/day then resets. Avoids pricing out but needs a separate "rolls today" counter + reset rule. | |
| Flat Energy cost | Fixed cost per roll, no escalation. Simplest but removes the spine's "escalating cost" pressure. | |
**User's choice:** Lifetime forgeCount curve

text: Q1 — How should roll→reveal→choose be modeled as commands?
raw:
### Q1 — How should roll→reveal→choose be modeled as commands?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Single atomic cmd + pure reveal | Reveal is a pure deterministic selector; ONE atomic run_forge command does pay + re-derive + validate chosen∈revealed + apply +level + increment forgeCount + append ONE history row. No pending state, no reload-mid-forge loss. | ✓ |
| Two-phase split (pending state) | run_forge pays+rolls+reveals into durable pending state; choose_forge_reward applies. Mirrors start/complete session but needs pending storage + migration + resume prompt. | |
| run_forge + install_module | run_forge rolls+reveals; reuse install_module for apply. But install_module installs a definitionId into a slot — doesn't fit upgrade-level semantics. | |
**User's choice:** Single atomic cmd + pure reveal

### Camera behavior
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Fixed framing | Fixed framing: Core centered, Cells arranged in rings around it, entire Flowgrid fits the viewport. If many Cells exist later, we re-tune then. Simplest, safest first slice (matches STACK.md's 'simple custom camera may be safer for the first slice'). | ✓ |

### Active state location
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Transient (memory only) | Active session lives only in client memory (Zustand store): { cellId, startedAt, accumulatedElapsedMs }. Reload drops it — user must restart. Completion calls a single `complete_focus_session` command using the accumulated duration. Simplest; matches Phase 1's atomic contract; loses in-progress sessions on reload/crash. | |
| Durable (persisted) | Active session is a durable record: write a pending SessionRecord on start, update accumulated time periodically (or on visibility change), finalize on finish, mark discarded on cancel. Survives reload. Adds a new durable entity/store and write amplification. | |
| Start-markered (resume prompt) | Transient in memory + a lightweight `activeSessionStartedAt` field on CellRecord (or a small ActiveSessionRecord) so reload shows 'You had a session in progress — resume or discard?' but doesn't checkpoint accumulated duration. Middle ground: one extra write on start, nothing during the session. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Start-markered (resume prompt)

answer: Diff for truth, tick for UI
options: Diff for truth, tick for UI
raw:
### Duration computation
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Wall-clock diff, injected | Compute durationSeconds at finish as `floor((finishedAt - startedAt) / 1000)` using injected `now` (from a clock abstraction the app provides). Real wall-clock drives the display timer in React, but the simulation command receives a deterministic IsoDateTime pair. Matches Phase 1 D-03/D-08. | |
| Client-side tick accumulator | Tick a stopwatch in the Zustand store every second using setInterval; pass accumulated seconds to `complete_focus_session`. UI timer is exact, but setInterval drift on backgrounded tabs could undercount. Recovery on resume = stored accumulated value. | |
| Diff for truth, tick for UI | Wall-clock diff for the durable command + a client-side tick only for UI display (decoupled). The simulation gets the precise diff; the UI timer is cosmetic. Resume on reload recomputes display from startedAt. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Diff for truth, tick for UI

### Cancel audit
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Cancel writes nothing | Cancel writes nothing durable — no SessionRecord, no operation, no audit row. Only effect is clearing the active-session marker. Strictest reading of SESS-03 ('without creating accidental rewards'). Phase 2 CONTEXT D-02 already chose 'rejected and not_implemented commands write nothing' — cancel aligns with that. | ✓ |
| Cancel = audit operation only | Cancel appends an operation row with `status: 'failed'` (or a new 'cancelled' status) for audit/sync, but no SessionRecord and no economy effects. Useful for 'I started this but bailed' analytics later. Adds enum value + repository write. | |
| Cancel = zero-reward session | Cancel writes a full SessionRecord with `durationSeconds: 0` and zero rewards, so the session history is complete and append-only. Matches 'completed sessions are append-only history' but pollutes history with non-effort. | |
**User's choice:** Cancel writes nothing

### Sub-second finish edge case
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Zero-reward session | Floor to 0 — a session finished in <1 second produces zero rewards and writes a SessionRecord with durationSeconds:0 and all gains at 0. Lets the history reflect the attempt. focusToCurrent already returns 0 for durationSeconds<=0. | |
| Treat as cancel | Treat finish-with-zero-duration as a cancel: no SessionRecord, no operation. Prevents empty sessions from cluttering history. Requires either a minimum-duration threshold or a 'no elapsed time' check. | ✓ |
| Reject sub-second finish | Reject finish with a validation issue if durationSeconds is 0; UI shows a 'Session too short to record' hint and forces a cancel. Consistent with Phase 1's reject-don't-throw pattern, but adds friction at the edge. | |
**User's choice:** Treat as cancel

### Create flow
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| create_cell command | New `create_cell` simulation command. Takes name, color, optional icon, dailyTargetSeconds; command generates the cellId, instantiates the four starter ModuleInstances + Output route to Core, and returns nextState with the new Cell. Output follows Phase 1 D-04 (default convert/store allocation). Keeps truth in simulation; repository diff-writes as usual. | ✓ |
| UI-built records | App shell builds the Cell record client-side (new cellId, starter modules, route) and writes it via a generic repository put. Faster path but violates 'simulation owns truth' and bypasses invariant validation. | |
| Command + factory helper | create_cell command + a deterministic starter-state factory variant that takes a cellId/name/dailyTarget and returns the four starter module instances + route to wire into an existing FlowgridSnapshot. Mirrors src/content/starter-state.ts but additive. | |
**User's choice:** create_cell command

### Record shape
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Add fields + Dexie v2 | Extend CellRecord with `color: string` (hex), `icon: string | null` (optional lucide name or emoji), and `archivedAt: IsoDateTimeString | null`. Migration bumps Dexie schema v1 -> v2 with a transform that defaults existing Cells to a starter color (e.g. '#6b7280'), icon: null, archivedAt: null. Aligns with Phase 2 D-08 (Dexie schema version bumps for shape changes). | ✓ |
| Split customization record | Add a separate `CellCustomizationRecord` keyed by cellId (color, icon) and `archivedAt` on CellRecord. Avoids coupling presentation to the gameplay record, but doubles the join cost on every Cell render. | |
| Archive in settings | Add color/icon to CellRecord but store archive as a separate `archivedCellIds` collection on a settings-like record. Awkward for sync and selection state. | |
**User's choice:** Add fields + Dexie v2

### Edit scope
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Identity + target only | Allow editing name, color, icon, and dailyTargetSeconds via an `edit_cell` command. xp, momentum, current, charge, activation, milestone progress, lastBloomLocalDate are NEVER editable from the UI — only by simulation. Preserves history integrity (Phase 2 D-09 / append-only session rule). | ✓ |
| Above + manual milestone reset | Above + allow manual reset of daily milestone progress (so a user can 'restart today'). Adds friction to the milestone promise and risks the Bloom-once-per-day rule (lastBloomLocalDate must still gate). | |
| All non-economy fields | Allow editing all 'identity' fields freely. Strict but less safe — typos on the form could rewrite economy values. Reject. | |
**User's choice:** Identity + target only

### Archive / delete posture
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Reversible archive only | Archive is fully reversible: `archive_cell` and `unarchive_cell` commands flip `archivedAt` to now (archive) or null (unarchive). Archived Cells hidden from the Flowgrid Home and Cell picker but visible in a History / Archived filter. Sessions, modules, routes preserved as-is. No deletion path. | |
| Archive + hard-delete (history-only) | Archive is reversible AND there is a separate hard-delete (gated, requires confirm) that wipes the Cell, its modules, its routes — but preserves SessionRecord rows (rewritten with a `cellNameAtDeletion` snapshot so history stays readable). More surface area, more edge cases. | |
| Archive now, delete deferred | Archive is reversible; deletion is a deferred-to-v2 feature (captured as deferred idea). Aligns with PROJECT.md ('Completed sessions are append-only real history') and keeps Phase 3 scope tight. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Archive now, delete deferred

### Rollover timing
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| App-open reconciliation | On app open (repository load -> snapshot), run a deterministic `reconcileDayRollover(snapshot, env)` pass before UI renders: for each Cell where lastBloomLocalDate < env.localDate, reset dailyMilestoneProgressSeconds to 0 and clear per-day Activation. Cells that didn't open the app yesterday simply look 'fresh today' (no penalty). Subsequent commands trust env.localDate as the current day. | |
| Lazy reset on next command | No app-open pass. Each command that touches a Cell (create/edit/start/finish) checks lastBloomLocalDate vs env.localDate; if stale, it resets milestone + activation inline. Simpler write path but the Flowgrid Home could briefly show yesterday's progress until a Cell is interacted with. | |
| Both | App-open pass for display-only state (so Home is correct on load) + invariant in each Cell-touching command (so simulation truth can't drift). Belt-and-suspenders. Most code, safest. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Both

### Momentum rule
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Monotonic up, no decay | Momentum only goes UP in Phase 3: +1 when Bloom fires (SIM-06), and freeze (no decay) otherwise. A missed day doesn't reduce Momentum — it just delays the next increment. Strictest reading of 'forgiving' and 'support return after missed days'. Initial value stays 0. | |
| Mild decay on miss | +1 on Bloom (SIM-06), and on app-open day-rollover if yesterday had no completed session for that Cell, Momentum decays by 1 (floor 0). Mild pressure, still recovers in one Bloom. Adds 'did-this-Cell-complete-yesterday' tracking. | ✓ |
| Streak with grace window | +1 on Bloom, +1 capped at e.g. 5 for each consecutive Bloom day; reset to 0 only after N consecutive missed days (grace window). Closer to a streak system but with grace. More state (lastActiveLocalDate, graceRemaining). | |
**User's choice:** Mild decay on miss

### Activation benefit
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| +% Current from Generator | While a Cell is Activated (Bloom fired today, lastBloomLocalDate == env.localDate), the Generator module produces +X% Current from focus time (e.g., +10%, matching gameplay-spine draft §14 example). The complete_focus_session command checks cell.activation > 0 and applies the bonus. Visible in the Cell inspector and on the hex (halo). | ✓ |
| Lower next milestone target | Activation reduces the daily milestone target for the next Bloom (e.g., -20% target while Activated), making it easier to chain days. Different feel — less Current, more 'keep the chain going'. | |
| +XP per minute | Activation boosts XP per minute instead of Current. Keeps Current/Charge/Energy identical to Phase 1 but accelerates local Cell identity growth. Less economy impact, more progression feel. | |
**User's choice:** +% Current from Generator

### Day-boundary derivation
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Settings.localDayBoundary | Use the existing `SettingsRecord.localDayBoundary` (default '00:00') and compute `localDate` from `now - boundary offset`. The injected `env.localDate` the simulation receives is already the resolved local date string. Day rollover checks compare this value. Lets users on odd schedules (e.g., '04:00' boundary) define 'today' their way. | ✓ |
| System local date only | Ignore localDayBoundary for Phase 3 and use the system local calendar date (toISOString().slice(0,10)). Simpler, but the existing Settings field becomes dead config until later. | |
| Boundary + once-per-day guard | Compute localDate from localDayBoundary AND expose a `todayVersusYesterday` helper that returns 'first-open-today' so the app-open reconciliation pass runs exactly once per real day even across rapid reloads. | |
**User's choice:** Settings.localDayBoundary

text: Q1 — How does Phase 2 import Sidecar's plugin interface for v1?
raw:
### Q1 — How does Phase 2 import Sidecar's plugin interface for v1?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Build inside sidecar | Plugin source lives at `~/.btca/agent/sandbox/sidecar/internal/plugins/gsd/` (matches tdmonitor/gitstatus/notes pattern). This repo keeps the read model + its tests; the plugin imports readmodel via a replace directive pointing at this repo. Runs in real Sidecar today, no bridge, no public-API upstream change. Cost: plugin source is in sidecar's tree, not this repo. | ✓ |
| Public plugin API | One-time change to sidecar: move `/internal/plugin` → `/plugin` (or add a public re-export package). Then this repo adds `require github.com/marcus/sidecar` and imports the plugin interface cleanly. Plugin source stays here. Cleanest separation, but it IS a sidecar-modification (small, one-time). | |
| Defer Sidecar registration | Phase 2 develops plugin logic against a local interface copy in this repo (`internal/hostiface`) + a fixture harness. Real Sidecar registration is deferred to Phase 5. PLUG-01 ("register and focus without breaking startup") is only proven via a mock host, not real Sidecar. Weakens the phase-2 success criterion. | |
**User's choice:** Build inside sidecar.

text: Q2 — How should sidecar consume the read model from this repo?
raw:
### Q2 — How should sidecar consume the read model from this repo?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Promote to public pkg | Move `internal/readmodel` → `pkg/readmodel` (or top-level `readmodel/`) in THIS repo. Sidecar's go.mod adds `require github.com/wvanderen/gsd-sidecar` + `replace … => /Users/eggfam/dev/gsd-sidecar`. Source stays here, no duplication, D-13's promotion trigger fires now. PKG-01 (v2) is effectively satisfied early by real consumer. | ✓ |
| Vendor into sidecar | Copy the read model source into sidecar's tree (e.g. `sidecar/internal/plugins/gsd/readmodel`). Single Go module, no cross-module import at all. But the read model now lives in two places, tests can drift, and Phase 1's fixture coverage gets forked. | |
| Inline into sidecar | Move both read model and plugin source into sidecar's tree entirely; this repo becomes planning-only (no Go). Maximizes simplicity for v1 runtime, but loses the module-isolation property Phase 1 established (D-12). | |
**User's choice:** Promote to public pkg.

text: Q3 — What shape should the always-visible Pulse take?
raw:
### Q3 — What shape should the always-visible Pulse take?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Single line, truncate | One terminal line, ordered: status glyph \| phase #/name \| plan \| progress % \| last-activity \| signal. Truncate right-to-left as width shrinks. Matches a HUD 'compact always-visible strip' feel; consistent with sidecar's terse footers. | ✓ |
| Two lines, grouped | Two lines: line 1 = status + phase #/name + plan; line 2 = progress bar + last-activity + strongest signal. More breathing room, each line stays readable at moderate widths, but eats a row and risks wrap at very narrow widths. | |
| Adaptive 1 or 2 lines | Single line at wide widths, automatically expand to two lines below a threshold (e.g. <80 cols). Most information-dense at every width, but two render paths to maintain and the threshold itself is a knob. | |
**User's choice:** Single line, truncate.

text: Q4 — How should status be visualized in Phase 2 Pulse?
raw:
### Q4 — How should status be visualized in Phase 2 Pulse?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Status-colored now | Phase 2 colors the status glyph from the model's Status field: blocked=red, executing=yellow, complete=green, planning=dim. Phase 3's UI-02 attention promotion then refines (e.g. red even when Status is 'executing' if a failed_check exists). Cheapest path to PROJECT.md's 'intervention over neutral'. | ✓ |
| Monochrome in P2 | Phase 2 renders Pulse monochrome with just a status word ('blocked', 'executing', etc.). Phase 3 introduces both color and attention promotion together. Tighter phase boundary, but loses the at-a-glance signal for all of Phase 2's demos. | |
| Glyph, no color | Phase 2 uses a status glyph without color (●=active, ◆=blocked, ✓=complete, …=planning). Shape carries some signal; color still deferred to Phase 3. | |
**User's choice:** Status-colored now.

text: Q5 — What fills the 'strongest signal' slot in Phase 2?
raw:
### Q5 — What fills the 'strongest signal' slot in Phase 2?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Highest diagnostic | Phase 2 fills the signal slot with the highest-severity Diagnostic already in the Phase 1 model (Error > Warn > Info). Operator sees something useful on day one; Phase 3 swaps in the proper attention-type pill once ATTN-01/02 land. Matches PROJECT.md 'promote intervention-relevant truth'. | ✓ |
| Empty slot in P2 | Phase 2 leaves the signal slot empty (or a dim placeholder like '—'). The pill appears properly in Phase 3 once attention is classified and priority-sorted. Tighter phase boundary, but Phase 2 Pulse demos lose the 'is intervention needed?' affordance that's the whole core value. | |
| Raw first fact | Phase 2 shows the first raw AttentionFact (Phase 1 emits Kinds like blocked_state/failed_check/deviation). Uses the model as-is, but Phase 1 facts aren't priority-sorted, so 'first' is document-order not urgency — Phase 3 replaces this with proper priority ordering. | |
**User's choice:** Highest diagnostic.

text: Q6 — What truncation priority at narrow widths?
raw:
### Q6 — What truncation priority at narrow widths?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Keep signal last | Order: status \| phase #/name \| plan \| progress % \| signal \| last-activity. Narrow widths drop activity first, then progress, then signal, keeping phase identity + intervention indicator longest. Matches 'core value is intervention awareness'. | ✓ |
| Drop signal first | Order: status \| phase #/name \| plan \| progress % \| last-activity \| signal. Narrow widths drop signal first, then activity, then progress, keeping phase identity + plan context longest. Matches the original proposal. | |

text: Q7 — What status glyph style for the Pulse first column?
raw:
### Q7 — What status glyph style for the Pulse first column?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Symbols | Symbol per status: ●=executing, ◆=blocked, ✓=complete, …=planning, ·=unknown. Visually distinct without English; compact. Sidecar's own footers use symbols (e.g. tab icons, git branch glyphs). | ✓ |
| Word | Short uppercase word: BLOCKED, ACTIVE, DONE, PLAN. Maximally clear; no legend needed. Costs 4-8 columns; at narrow widths the word itself becomes the first thing truncated against. | |
| Letter | Status-colored single letter: B (red), A (yellow), C (green), P (dim). One column; takes color well; needs a brief mental legend but operators internalize it fast. | |

text: Q8 — How should Pulse show progress?
raw:
### Q8 — How should Pulse show progress?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Plans fraction | Plans fraction only: '3/5 plans' (or '18/25'). Denominator visible — operator sees scope at a glance. Phase count implicit in the ladder below. | ✓ |
| Percent | Percent only: '60%'. Most compact. Loses absolute scope (is '60%' of 5 plans or 25?). | |
| Fraction + pct | Plans fraction + percent in parens: '3/5 (60%)'. Maximally informative for one extra column pair. | |

text: Q9 — How should Pulse render last-activity?
raw:
### Q9 — How should Pulse render last-activity?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Relative | Relative: '2h ago', '5d ago', 'just now'. Operator-relevant (recency > exact date); needs a small relative-time helper. LastActivityDesc (free-text like 'Phase 01 complete') drops first when width shrinks. | ✓ |
| Absolute short | Absolute short: '06-28' or 'Jun 28'. Compact, unambiguous, no formatter beyond date parse. Loses the qualitative 'how recent' affordance. | |
| Relative + desc | Relative + desc: '2h ago · Phase 01 complete'. Uses both LastActivity and LastActivityDesc at wide widths; drops desc first at narrow. Adds ~25 cols when desc present. | |
**User's choice:** Relative.

text: Q10 — How should Phase 2 handle the plan ladder when there are more plans than rows (flowgrid = 25)?
raw:
### Q10 — How should Phase 2 handle the plan ladder when there are more plans than rows (flowgrid = 25)?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Truncate + hint | Phase 2 renders the first N plans that fit in the available height after Pulse, with a dim footer '+N more plans (navigation in Phase 4)'. PLUG-04 (j/k + viewport scroll) is explicitly Phase 4. Tightest phase boundary; flowgrid's 25 plans shows ~10-15 in Phase 2. | ✓ |
| Viewport now | Phase 2 implements a viewport slice [offset, offset+height] with a selection cursor even though j/k keys land in Phase 4. Front-loads PLUG-04 scroll work; weakens phase boundary but means Phase 4 only adds key handlers. | |
| Compress to fit | Phase 2 fits all plans by compressing rows (e.g. drop to 1-line compact rows when count > height). No scroll needed; no truncation. But compression at 25 plans means ~2-3 cols per row, unreadable. | |
**User's choice:** Truncate + hint.

text: Q12 — What triggers PLUG-03 reloads in Phase 2?
raw:
### Q12 — What triggers PLUG-03 reloads in Phase 2?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Focus + manual only | Reload on PluginFocusedMsg (focus-gained) + on manual refresh command (the one Phase 2 command). No polling, no event bus. Cheapest; matches PROJECT.md 'inspection-first' and Phase 1 deferral of file-watching (WATCH-01 = v2). Operator hits 'r' or re-focuses the tab to see new state. | ✓ |
| + slow poll | Focus + manual + slow poll (e.g. every 30s). Catches background agent progress without operator action; still cheap (Load is fast, local, pure file reads). Adds a periodic timer command like tdmonitor's pattern. | |
| + event bus watch | Focus + manual + event bus subscription on file-watcher events. Lowest latency; but Phase 1 CONTEXT explicitly deferred file-watching to v2 WATCH-01. Pulls v2 work into Phase 2. | |
**User's choice:** Focus + manual only.

raw:
### Q4: SECR-05 在 Phase 1 里怎么记？
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 部分覆盖 + 显式跳过项 | 只断言目录 700；凭据 600 打印为跳过项但不计失败 | ✓ |

**User's choice:** 部分覆盖 + 显式跳过项

### 首字节预算
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 15s | 紧凑，但它量的是「连接+排队+模型开始输出」。带推理的模型在首 token 前静默 10s 以上是常态，15s 会把「慢」判成「断」 | |
| 30s | 留出推理模型的沉默期，同时仍远短于「用户会去按取消」的阈值。超过 30s 的沉默面板和卡死无法区分 | ✓ |
| 60s | 几乎不会误判，代价是真挂死的供应商要用户等半分钟才看到错误 | |
| 你定 | 先做一个常量，实测几个真实供应商后再定 | |
**User's choice:** 30s

### 块间停顿预算
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 20s | 对真卡死反应快。SSE 在 ~10–30 chunk/s，正常流几乎不会静默 20s；但长思考/长工具间隙会误杀 | |
| 45s | 比首字节预算宽（这是有意的：已经证明连接活着，所以容忍度应该更高），又不至于让用户以为卡死 | ✓ |
| 90s | 基本只抓「供应商彻底掉了」，代价是真卡死时用户会先去按取消 | |
| 你定 | 与首字节预算同一个数值，少一个旋钮 | |
**User's choice:** 45s

text: keep-alive 是否重置停顿计时器
raw:
### keep-alive 是否重置停顿计时器
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 不重置预算 | 注释/空 data 帧只证明连接活着。若重置预算，一个「发 keep-alive 但模型卡住」的供应商就永远不会超时——而那正是本需求要抓的形状。代价：有些代理真的只靠注释保持连接 | ✓ |
| 重置停顿预算 | 连接还活着就不算卡死。代价：卡死永远不报，用户只能靠取消退出（正是 ROADMAP 成功标准 3 想避免的） | |
| 重置+总预算封顶 | keep-alive 重置停顿、不重置首字节；另加一个硬总预算封顶。多一个旋钮，但两个风险都盖住 | |
**User's choice:** 不重置预算

### 两个预算的存放形式
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 常量 + 可注入 | 两个预算写在 `Chat.js` 的常量里，`Transport` 允许调用方注入覆盖值。生产用默认，测试传 300ms。一次投入，Phase 5 的「每供应商超时」直接接上 | ✓ |
| 只写常量 | 最简单，但测试要等真实秒数，或者只能靠改源码来测。超时那一条就会从每提交门里消失 | |
| 进 dev 配置 | 跟供应商一起走 dev 配置，Phase 2 就把它当配置项。代价：Phase 2 还没有配置层，得先造一个小的 | |
**User's choice:** 常量 + 可注入

### 什么算「正常结束」
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 两个信号任一 | `[DONE]`/`message_stop` 或 `finish_reason`/`stop_reason` 任一存在即算正常结束；两者都无才报「提前结束」。兼容不发 [DONE] 的端点，同时仍能抓「连 finish_reason 都没有」的真截断 | ✓ |
| 只认终止标记 | 只认 `[DONE]`/`message_stop`。能多抓一种情形：代理在最后一个 chunk 后、终止标记前把连接截了。代价：任何不发终止标记的兼容端点全部误报 | |
| 只认 finish_reason | 终止标记当冗余信息忽略。最简单，但把「连接被代理截断」和「供应商正常结束」合并成一种 | |
**User's choice:** 两个信号任一

### `stop_reason` / `finish_reason` 的处理程度
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 映射成文案 | `refusal`（HTTP 200、流干净、但零文本）与 `max_tokens`（真截断）各自给一句可读文案。PITFALLS P12 把「空回答无解释」列为本产品类最坏失败模式 | ✓ |
| 只显示原值 | 不做文案映射，只把原始值显示出来。实现最小，但用户看到 `max_tokens` 得自己知道那是什么意思 | |
| 留到 Phase 3 | 本阶段只保证流式与错误分类，停止原因的文案留给 Phase 3 的转录。风险：Phase 2 的 UAT 会看到空白回答而无法解释 | |
**User's choice:** 映射成文案

### 三类异常结局的呈现
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 文本下方一行标注 | 已收到的文本原样留着，下方一行小字（「已取消」/「提前结束」/「超时」/错误原因）。每个回答自带它的结局，Phase 3 的 append-only 块模型直接继承这个形状 | ✓ |
| 复用顶部状态行 | 复用 ROADMAP 成功标准 1 已有的「生成中 / 已用时长」那一行，把它变成状态行。少一个控件，但换到下一个回答时结局就消失了 | |
**User's choice:** 文本下方一行标注

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Infer from cask metadata | Analyze description/name text with keyword matching or embeddings to infer categories. Auto-categorizes all casks. May have misclassifications. | |
| Manual mapping file | Create a manual mapping file (e.g., cask-categories.json) with token→category assignments. Precise but requires curation. Unmapped casks go to 'Uncategorized'. | |
| Import from Homebrew data | Check if Homebrew's API or cask JSON includes category/tag fields we can import. Canonical source but may not match our taxonomy. | ✓ |
| Hybrid approach | Hybrid: start with Homebrew tags if available, supplement with keyword inference for unmapped casks, allow manual overrides. | |
**User's choice:** Check if homebrew has something, else, we can do a small model run it locally via AWS Bedrock connection that I have that can categorize it and save it.

### Question 2: Category Granularity
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 8-10 broad categories | Developer Tools, Productivity, Design, Media, Games, Utilities, Communication, Education, Other. Matches common App Store taxonomies. | |
| 15-20 specific categories | More granular: Web Browsers, Code Editors, Video Players, Graphic Design, Password Managers, etc. Better discovery but longer filter UI. | |
| Let the model decide | Let Bedrock determine category set organically from the cask descriptions (unsupervised clustering). May surface unexpected but useful groupings. | ✓ |
**User's choice:** Let the model decide

### Question 1: UI Location
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Browse page (local) | Filter pills/buttons above the card grid on /browse page. Sort dropdown next to it. Clean separation of controls from nav. | ✓ |
| Header (global) | Category tabs in header (global). Persists across pages. More prominent but takes header space alongside search. | |
| Sidebar (desktop-only) | Left sidebar with category checkboxes + sort radio buttons. Desktop-friendly but breaks mobile layout or needs hamburger menu. | |
**User's choice:** Browse page (local) (Recommended)

### Question 2: State Persistence
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| URL query params | URL like /browse?category=developer-tools&sort=alphabetical. ISR-friendly, shareable links, back button works correctly. | ✓ |
| Client-side state only | Client-side React state only. Fast switching, no page reload, but breaks shareable links and ISR caching. | |
| Shallow routing (hybrid) | Use Next.js shallow routing to update URL without triggering server render. Best of both but more complex. | |
**User's choice:** URL query params (Recommended)

### Question 1: Detail Page Placement
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Dedicated GitHub stats card | Prominent card/block below the install command with star/fork/issue counts and GitHub logo. Clear social proof. | ✓ |
| Inline metadata row | Small inline stats strip alongside version/homepage in the existing metadata section. Subtle, doesn't add vertical space. | |
| Sidebar stats panel | Right sidebar (if you add one) with GitHub stats, dependencies, etc. Separates metadata from main content. | |
**User's choice:** Dedicated GitHub stats card (Recommended)

### Question 2: Metrics to Display
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| All three metrics | Show all three metrics (stars, forks, issues) with icons. Complete picture of repo health. | ✓ |
| Stars only | Just stars — most recognizable social proof signal. Simpler, less cluttered. | |
| Stars + issues | Stars + issues. Stars show popularity, issues show activity/support burden. Skip forks (less relevant for end users). | |
**User's choice:** All three metrics

## GitHub Stats on Cards
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Yes, add star count badge | Add a star count pill next to the existing install count pill on cards. Shows social proof at-a-glance. Only for casks with GitHub data. | ✓ |
| No, detail page only | Keep cards clean — stats are detail-page-only. Cards already show install count; adding stars clutters the metadata strip. | |
| GitHub icon indicator only | Add a subtle GitHub icon/indicator (no number) to cards that have GitHub repos. Signals 'this has stats' without adding numbers. | |
**User's choice:** Yes, add star count badge (Recommended)

### Question 1: Back-Button Behavior
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Full state restoration | Browser back button should restore the exact page/filter/sort state you left from. Use scroll restoration and URL state. | ✓ |
| URL state only, no scroll | Back button works but doesn't restore scroll position. Simpler but less polished. | |
| Client-side routing + history API | Use client-side routing (next/navigation) with scroll restoration and history state. More complex but smoothest UX. | |
**User's choice:** Full state restoration (Recommended)

### Question 2: Perceived Lag Fix
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Loading skeletons (Phase 3 pattern) | Add loading skeletons for pagination transitions (Phase 3 added them for search). Gives instant feedback while ISR loads. | ✓ |
| Prefetch adjacent pages | Use Next.js `<Link prefetch>` to preload adjacent pages on hover. Page transitions feel instant. | |
| Skeletons + prefetch | Both: skeletons for slow transitions + prefetch for fast ones. Best UX but more complexity. | |
**User's choice:** Loading skeletons (Phase 3 pattern)

## Layout Width
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Responsive grid 1/2/3/4 cols | Mobile: 1 col, Tablet: 2 cols, Desktop (1024px+): 3 cols, Wide (1440px+): 4 cols. Adapts to screen size. | ✓ |
| Cap at 3 columns max | Mobile: 1 col, Tablet: 2 cols, Desktop: 3 cols. Stop at 3 to keep cards larger on ultra-wide displays. | |
| 3 cols with max-width container | Add a max-width container (1400px) so the grid doesn't stretch infinitely on wide screens. 3 cols within the container. | |
**User's choice:** Responsive grid 1/2/3/4 cols (Recommended)

## Cron Frequency
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Daily | Homebrew publishes once per day — more frequent syncs get stale data. Hobby plan covers this. Zero additional cost. | ✓ |
| Every 6 hours | Catches mid-day Homebrew republishes faster. Requires Vercel Pro (~$20/mo). | |
| On-demand only | Manual trigger via authenticated HTTP call. Not a production strategy. | |
**User's choice:** Daily

raw:
### Q3: Error handling for inaccessible repos
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Mark github_enriched=false, skip | Log failure, leave stats as NULL. Next sync retries. | ✓ |
| Retry immediately with backoff | Adds latency; 404s won't resolve on retry. | |
**User's choice:** Mark as github_enriched=false, skip gracefully

### Q1: Table structure
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Single flat casks table | All fields inline, no joins. Simple queries. | ✓ |
| Normalized (casks + install_counts + github_stats) | Cleaner relational model, adds JOIN complexity for every query. | |
**User's choice:** Single flat casks table

### Q2: Field set
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Core only | name, token, description, version, homepage, icon_url, install counts, GitHub stats. | ✓ |
| Extended | Also include categories, platform_compatibility, caveats, bottle_url now. | |
**User's choice:** Core fields only

### Q1: Update mechanism
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Upsert on token | INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (token) DO UPDATE. Idempotent, fast, safe. | ✓ |
| Full replace (truncate + reinsert) | Simple but table is briefly empty mid-run; ISR serves stale data. | |
| Diff-only (skip unchanged) | Most efficient; requires checksum strategy since Homebrew has no per-cask updatedAt. | |
**User's choice:** Upsert on token

### Q2: Handling removed casks
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Soft-delete (set is_active=false, keep row) | Prevents ISR page 404s during Homebrew temporary unpublish. | ✓ |
| Hard-delete immediately | Simple but risks stale ISR pages for popular casks temporarily removed. | |
**User's choice:** Soft-delete

### Q3: ISR cache invalidation
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| revalidateTag('casks') post-sync | ISR pages reflect new data as soon as the sync completes. | ✓ |
| Rely on ISR TTL | Browse pages could show day-old data for hours post-sync. | |
**User's choice:** revalidateTag immediately post-sync

**User's choice:** II. Per-bucket explicit

### Refined approach
| Mechanism | Description | Selected |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Subpath exports + static rule | Foundation `src/` is split into `external/` (public) and `internal/` (primitives). `package.json` `exports` field declares `.` and `./internal` subpaths. ONE `no-restricted-imports` rule blocks `@email-platform/foundation/internal*` from `apps/*/src/*.module.ts`. ONE override allows it in `apps/*/src/infrastructure/**/*.ts`. Adding new primitives in future phases never requires editing `.eslintrc.js` — only correct file placement. | ✓ |
| Specific ESLint list (option A from initial presentation) | Hard-coded list of forbidden symbols (`S3CoreModule`, `BucketStorageModule`). Must be extended manually for every future infra primitive. | |
| Generic ESLint whitelist (option C from initial presentation) | Long regex of allowed symbols. Maintained in `.eslintrc.js`, requires updates per phase. | |
| Convention-only (option B from initial presentation) | Documentation + code review only, no enforcement. | |

text: Does set_difficulty also reset the board?
raw:
### Does set_difficulty also reset the board?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Pure setter | set_difficulty only stores the new level. Phase 14 JS calls game.reset() separately. Clean separation of concerns. | ✓ |
| Auto-reset the board | set_difficulty updates the level AND resets the game board internally. Phase 14 JS only needs one call. But it bakes a UI policy into the Rust layer. | |
**User's choice:** Pure setter

### Does reset() preserve difficulty?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Persist across resets | difficulty stored on WasmGame, not on Game. reset() only reinitializes inner Game board. Phase 14 doesn't need to re-apply after every game. | ✓ |
| Reset to Medium | reset() also clears difficulty back to 1. Phase 14 JS must call set_difficulty again after every reset. | |
**User's choice:** Persist across resets

### Default difficulty on WasmGame::new()?
| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Medium (1) | Matches existing behavior before Phase 13. Satisfies UI-03 (first-visit default is Medium). | ✓ |
| Easy (0) | Starts friendlier but doesn't match UI-03. | |
**User's choice:** Medium (1)

| Hardcode Medium | Update the one call site to pass difficulty=1. CLI behavior stays identical to today. | ✓ |

**User's choice:** Update all to pass difficulty=1
